title: Calculating Various Types of Employees' Gross Pay

back: [[imp:Total earnings before any deductions.]]
For hourly workers: Gross pay = Hours × Rate.
Includes regular hours, overtime, commissions, bonuses.

cards.front: How is [[kw:overtime pay]] calculated for non‑exempt hourly workers?
back: [[imp:Overtime rate = Regular hourly rate × 1.5.]]
Overtime pay = Overtime hours × Overtime rate.
Regular hours are usually 40 per week; hours beyond 40 are overtime.
$$\text{Gross Pay} = (40 \times \text{Hourly Rate}) + (\text{OT Hours} \times (\text{Hourly Rate} \times 1.5))$$
cards.front: Give the formula for gross pay with overtime.

back: Employees are paid a fixed amount for each good unit produced.
$$\text{Gross Pay} = \text{Units Produced} \times \text{Rate per Unit}$$
Defective units are not paid.
Different piece rates apply to different production levels.
[[imp:Only the units in each tier are paid at that tier's rate.]]
Example: first 50 at $0.50, next 100 at $0.62, etc.

cards.front: How do you calculate gross pay under a differential schedule?
back: Multiply the number of units in each tier by its tier rate, then sum all tiers.
$$\text{Gross Pay} = \sum (\text{Units in Tier} \times \text{Tier Rate})$$
Always start from the first tier and work upward.
Pay is a percent of the salesperson's net sales.
$$\text{Commission} = \text{Net Sales} \times \text{Commission Rate}$$
No base salary; earnings vary directly with sales.
[[imp:A draw is an advance against future commissions.]]
Final pay = Commission Earned − Draw.
If commission < draw, the salesperson may owe the difference.

cards.front: A salesperson earns 8% commission on $12,000 net sales and draws $600. Compute final pay.

back: A fixed salary plus a commission on sales.
$$\text{Gross Pay} = \text{Salary} + (\text{Sales} \times \text{Commission Rate})$$
Provides a base income plus sales incentive.
Commission rates increase as sales reach higher tiers.
Similar to differential pay, but applied to sales dollars.
Example: 4% on first $20,000, 7% on excess.

cards.front: A salesperson gets $2,000 salary, plus 3% on sales up to $20,000 and 6% above. Sales are $28,000. Find gross pay.
